name: buttondown-email-sent-to-notion-newsletter
replaces_classic_zap: Newsletter Sent -> Update Status in Notion

trigger.notes: Polling trigger on the official Buttondown app, connection `workflowers`. Fires for EVERY email Buttondown sends, not only ones drafted from Notion — see the skip path. Durable triggers cannot set a polling interval, so any custom interval on the classic Zap was silently dropped at migration.

connection_notes.TableCLIAPI: search/find_record against Zapier Table 01KNJN2MSBAJVXRME6M1Y65F5B — Zapier Tables need no connection and cost no tasks.

notion.properties_written: Status (status) -> "Sent"; Send Date (date) via `properties|||Send Date|||date__start`, which requires use_zapier_datetime_fields: true alongside it
notion.template_mode: N/A — this updates an existing page and never creates one, so repo rule 5 does not apply

zapier_table.name: Email Newsletter ID Mapping

fields.f1: Page ID (Notion Newsletter Issues page id)

zapier_table.result_shape: find_record wraps each hit as {new, old, record_id, table_id} — values at data[0].old.data.<fieldId> — and returns {data: []} on a miss.

fixes_applied_vs_classic_zap: Empty-lookup guard. The classic Zap set `_zap_search_success_on_miss: false`, which halts on a miss. A durable reading `data[0].old.data.f1` unguarded would throw and burn all five step retries — exactly the bug that cost update-notion-when-rescheduled-in-buttondown 100% of its runs. Since the trigger fires for every Buttondown send, a miss is a routine non-event: it logs and returns `{skipped: "no-notion-page-for-email"}`.
publish_date is optional. A send event without one now still marks the issue Sent rather than failing; the classic Zap would have written an empty date.
A payload with no email id still throws, naming the keys it received.
Returns only ids rather than the Notion action's echo of the entire page, which keeps the step checkpoint small.

relationship_to_sibling_zaps.notion-newsletter-to-buttondown: The outbound leg. Creates the Buttondown draft/scheduled email from the Notion page and writes the mapping row this Zap reads.
relationship_to_sibling_zaps.update-notion-when-rescheduled-in-button: Writes the same `Send Date` property off the `new_email_reschedule` trigger. No conflict: that one fires while the email is still scheduled, this one when it actually sends, and both write the same value from the same source. This Zap additionally sets Status.
